title: Programming & Numerical Methods for Bioengineering
description: Reproducible scientific computing, data structures, visualization, numerical integration, model fitting, and error analysis for experimental and engineered systems.

outcomes.description: Write modular code with explicit inputs and outputs.
Select numerical methods and diagnose error.
Fit models without confusing interpolation and validation.
Make reproducible plots and document data provenance.

lesson_objectives.description: Represent observations with explicit units and metadata.
Write small functions that can be checked independently.
Implement a time step and compare solver resolution.
Track stability and conservation constraints.
Separate model fitting from model validation.
Inspect residuals and quantify parameter uncertainty.
Choose a plot that matches variable type and comparison.
Show distributions and uncertainty without obscuring individual observations.
Write known-answer tests for a small scientific function, computing the expected values independently.
Choose a tolerance and explain why floating-point numbers are compared with a tolerance.
Make a stochastic analysis repeatable and record the provenance needed to reproduce a figure.
Count the operations of simple loops and express their growth with big-O notation.
Estimate run time from an operation count and a stated rate, and predict how it scales when the input grows.
Choose data structures and algorithms (hash-based lookup, sorting with binary search, vectorized operations) that change the scaling, and decide when optimization is worth it.
Explain machine epsilon and compute the spacing between representable floating-point numbers near a given value.
Diagnose catastrophic cancellation, estimate the digits lost, and choose a numerically stable formula.
Write comparisons and tests with appropriate absolute and relative tolerances.
Trace concentration functions with explicit units and domain checks.
Classify missing, malformed and nonfinite records under a declared contract.
Separate parsing, pure calculation and auditable reporting.
Predict array broadcast shapes and selected entries.
Distinguish axis reductions, paired changes and outer comparisons.
Estimate storage and preserve input arrays when transforming data.
Trace valid root brackets and midpoint error bounds.
Diagnose continuity and equation-scaling limits on root convergence.
Evaluate Newton updates against domains and derivative information.
Calculate quadrature on explicit uniform and nonuniform grids.
Evaluate refinement-based error estimates under a stated order model.
Distinguish solver stability, positivity and accuracy.
Calculate and verify a centered affine least-squares fit.
Diagnose rank loss and residual degrees of freedom.
Distinguish numerical stability from statistical validation.
Calculate threshold metrics with explicit denominators.
Choose splits and preprocessing that respect a prediction target.
Document model selection and reproducible final evaluation.
Filter and summarize records under explicit unit and finite-value contracts.
Calculate frozen held-out threshold metrics with explicit denominators.
Evaluate group separation, exclusions and classifier case evidence.

modules.title: Data structures, units, and reproducible code

lessons.title: Data structures, units, and reproducible code
lessons.worked_example: Store each sample's treatment, donor, batch, and measurement unit together; keep the raw file unchanged and write cleaned outputs as a derived artifact.

lessons.title: Numerical integration and differential models
lessons.worked_example: Integrating ẋ=−x from 0 to 1 with Euler step h=0.1 gives a different result than h=0.01; convergence toward e⁻¹ is the check.

lessons.title: Regression, uncertainty, and validation
lessons.worked_example: A model with lower training error but higher held-out error may be overfit; simplify it, regularize it, or collect independent data.

lessons.title: Visualization and uncertainty communication
lessons.worked_example: Plotting donor-level points with a paired line can make within-donor treatment effects clearer than two unpaired bars when donors are the randomized blocks.

lessons.title: Testing a scientific function: known answers, tolerances, seeds and provenance
lessons.worked_example: doubling_time_hours(1e5, 8e5, 30) is 10 hours (three doublings); the culture growing from 2.0×10⁵ to 1.28×10⁶ cells in 24 h has a doubling time of 8.96 h, and (0.1 + 0.2) − 0.3 is 5.55e-17, which is why floats are compared with a tolerance.

lessons.title: How long will it take? Algorithmic cost, scaling and choosing data structures for research code
lessons.worked_example: All pairs of 10,000 items is 49,995,000 comparisons, about 5.0 s at a synthetic 10⁷ per second and 100 times longer for 10 times the data; 10,000 list lookups in 1,000,000 items cost about 5.0×10⁹ comparisons, while a set makes each lookup constant time.

lessons.title: Floating-point arithmetic in scientific code: rounding, cancellation and comparing numbers safely
lessons.worked_example: Near 10⁸ doubles are spaced about 2.2×10⁻⁸ apart; the shortcut variance of three values near 10⁸ returns 0.0 although the true value is 0.6667, a loss of about 16 digits; the two-pass formula gives the right answer.

modules.title: Input contracts, parsing and pure scientific functions

lessons.title: Input contracts, parsing and pure scientific functions
lessons.worked_example:
A synthetic record reports mass 1.5 mg and volume 500 uL. Convert volume to 0.5 mL, then calculate 1.5/0.5=3 mg/mL. The equivalent record in mL must give the same answer. Scaling both mass and volume by two gives 3/1=3 mg/mL, another invariant. Scaling only mass by two doubles the result; these are useful tests because they check the meaning of the calculation rather than copying its internal statements.

Suppose a six-row file has two valid records, one blank mass, one zero volume, one `nan` mass and one unknown unit. The declared policy accepts two rows and quarantines four with distinct reasons. Computing a mean requires reporting both the accepted count and the exclusions. A report that says only “mean concentration 3” hides whether that value came from two observations or all six. Its denominator is part of the evidence.

For a separate synthetic calibration, convert a reading of 2.4 arbitrary units using baseline 0.4 and scale 2 arbitrary units per mg/mL. The corrected concentration is (2.4−0.4)/2=1 mg/mL. Applying this correction before parsing, or forgetting the baseline, changes the scientific meaning even if the code runs without exceptions.

modules.title: Array shapes, broadcasting and memory-aware reductions

lessons.title: Array shapes, broadcasting and memory-aware reductions
lessons.worked_example:
Compare sample corrections [1,2,3] against the same 3-by-2 signal matrix. Convert them to a column and subtract to get [9,99], [12,102] and [15,105]. The overall mean becomes 57. Using channel baselines instead gave overall mean four. These are different operations with different metadata, not competing estimates of one quantity. A shape assertion plus a hand-check of the first and last row can distinguish them.

A slice may share storage with its parent array. If a preprocessing stage needs an independent buffer, an explicit copy avoids changing the raw matrix through a view. Checking that the original signal remains unchanged after transformation provides a behavioral test; merely checking a variable name such as `cleaned` does not prove independence. An advanced-index selection often copies, while basic slicing often returns a view, so the actual operation matters.

lessons.title: Root brackets, residuals and conditioning
lessons.worked_example:
Use f(x)=x²−2 on [1,2]. The first midpoint 1.5 has positive residual, so retain [1,1.5]. The next midpoint 1.25 has negative residual, so retain [1.25,1.5]. After two halvings the width is 0.25 and the final midpoint is 1.375, with a location bound 0.125. Its actual error from √2 is about 0.039214, smaller than the bound.

Starting instead with [0,4], eight halvings give width 4/256=0.015625 and final-midpoint error bound 0.0078125. To guarantee a bound no greater than 0.001, solve 4/2^(k+1)≤0.001. The minimum integer k is eleven. These bounds require the valid root-containing interval to be preserved at every update. They are deterministic algorithmic guarantees, not confidence intervals for an estimated physical parameter.

modules.title: Quadrature, step error and stability checks

lessons.title: Quadrature, step error and stability checks
lessons.worked_example:
Three nonuniform synthetic observations at times [0,1,3] seconds have rates [0,2,2] mg/s. The first area is one mg and the second is four mg, so total area is five mg. Replacing both interval widths by one second gives three mg and incorrectly shortens the experiment. Plotting the points and intervals makes the difference visible before choosing a method.

For Euler with λ=2 and h=0.1, ten steps yield 0.8¹⁰≈0.107374 after one second. Halving h gives 0.9²⁰≈0.121577, closer to exp(−2). The refinement difference is about 0.014202. A first-order estimate uses divisor one, but the exact fine-grid error is about 0.013759: the leading-order estimate is approximate at these finite steps. Report that distinction rather than calling the refinement difference a measured uncertainty interval.

modules.title: Least squares, rank and scaled coordinates

lessons.title: Least squares, rank and scaled coordinates
lessons.worked_example:
For z=[−1,0,1] and y=[2,3,5], the mean response is 10/3 and slope is 1.5. Predictions are [11/6,10/3,29/6], with residuals [1/6,−1/3,1/6]. Their sum is zero, and their dot product with z is zero. These orthogonality checks follow from the least-squares conditions and provide a separate way to assess the fit. Sum of squared residuals is 1/6.

There are three observations and two fitted coefficients, so residual degrees of freedom are one. A residual standard error computed as sqrt(SSE/(n−p)) is sqrt(1/6)≈0.408248. That quantity requires an appropriate error model to support inference. It is neither a held-out prediction score nor an automatic confidence interval. A line with two observations has no residual degrees of freedom for this estimate even if it fits exactly.

Now label x as [100000001,100000002,100000003] and z=x−100000002. The centered fit still has slope 1.5 and centered intercept 10/3. The uncentered intercept is approximately −149999999.666667. Its huge magnitude reflects the remote origin, not a large local measured response. Reporting the centered equation makes the observed-domain meaning clearer.

The preserved floating-point lesson estimates spacing near 10⁸ using |x| times epsilon. That is a scale estimate, not the exact adjacent-float spacing. In binary64, 10⁸ lies in the binade [2²⁶,2²⁷), so spacing is 2^(26−52)=2⁻²⁶≈1.490116×10⁻⁸. The existing approximate question and key are preserved. Distinguishing the exact binade value prevents treating the approximation as a library result.

modules.title: Grouped validation, thresholds and reproducible reports

lessons.title: Grouped validation, thresholds and reproducible reports
lessons.worked_example:
Eight synthetic observations have labels [1,0,1,0,0,1,0,0] and scores [0.9,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5,0.4,0.3,0.2]. At threshold 0.5 with equality positive, TP=2, FP=3, FN=1 and TN=2. Sensitivity is 2/3, precision is 2/5, specificity is 2/5 and accuracy is 4/8. F1, defined as 2TP/(2TP+FP+FN), is 0.5.

At threshold 0.7, TP stays two while FP falls to one, FN stays one and TN rises to four. Accuracy becomes 6/8=0.75 and precision becomes 2/3. This synthetic comparison illustrates threshold effects; it supplies no decision cost or validated threshold for a real setting. Choosing 0.7 only because this small evaluation table looks better would turn the table into selection data.

Now assign two adjacent records to each of four donors. A split placing each donor's first record in training and second in evaluation has four overlapping donors, even though row identifiers are unique. A split keeping donors one and two in training and donors three and four in evaluation has no donor overlap. It has fewer independent groups than rows, and does not establish generalization to another site or future time.

## Reproducibility is a chain of artifacts

Record immutable raw inputs, parsing and exclusion rules, split assignments, training-only transformations, code revision, dependency versions, candidate-selection procedure and final threshold. A pseudorandom seed alone does not specify the algorithm, software version or order of inputs. Preserve split identifiers directly when exact reconstruction matters. A plot should expose counts, units, threshold and grouping rather than present a single score without context.

Keep the final evaluation report separate from exploratory selection reports. If the final set is consulted to change the model, disclose that use and treat its later score accordingly. Reproducible leakage is still leakage; provenance allows it to be detected, not excused.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added an original lesson on testing a scientific function (known-answer tests, floating-point tolerances, seeded randomness and provenance records) with six formative items with computed keys and four retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Added two original lessons (algorithmic cost, scaling and data structures; floating-point rounding, cancellation and safe comparison) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a common-mistakes section to 1 original lesson that lacked one (programming-5); each bullet names a mistake that the lesson's own text addresses. Fixed number formatting that an earlier authoring step left in learner-visible text: raw exponent notation (a number written with the letter e and a power of ten) and floating-point artifacts (a decimal with a long run of trailing digits) in the floating-point reading (Python output now in a code span), the testing reading (Python literals now in code spans). No answer key, tolerance or objective changed. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added six original lessons on contracts/parsing/pure functions, array axes/broadcasting/memory, roots/conditioning, quadrature/stability, least-squares rank/scaling and grouped validation; a synthetic pipeline lab and proposed 14-week schedule. Developed with Codex assistance. Still partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

limitations: Four compact prototype readings remain beside nine substantial original lessons and one synthetic pipeline lab; this is not a full university semester.
Proposed weekly structure is unmeasured and unreviewed; graded homework, exams, full labs and a cumulative graded project remain absent.
Examples, functions, observations, labels and classifier scores are synthetic; no actual experimental or classifier utility evidence is established.
Of 54 numeric items, two preserved items require units; none enforces significant figures or dimensions. New numeric items request bare numbers in explicit scales.
Learner code execution remains disabled. Choices, numerical outputs and CSV cells do not grade implementations, exception handling, essays or plots.
The preserved spacing key is the approximate |x| times epsilon scale; lesson 12 distinguishes exact binade spacing near 10⁸ without changing the preserved item.
Qualified subject, code, accessibility and workload review remain absent. Public formative keys and practice points are not course grades.
Five official documentation pages were retrieved link-only; no teaching prose, code example, figure or dataset was imported.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments, a full laboratory sequence, a cumulative graded project, measured workload and qualified human review remain outstanding.
